This is the strongest citation of the four, and it survived the hardest attack I could make on it. The attack was the right one to try: a modern-spelling Bacon is exactly where an editor silently normalises capitals, and the sentence is one that most texts run on from But to speak in a mean, which would make a capital T at the head of the quotation a minted word.

WHAT I DID. I did not read the Wikisource page as a web page. I pulled the raw wikitext of Page:Essays_of_Francis_Bacon_1908_Scott.djvu/133 and read the transcription of the scan directly. Its running head is the proof of the page number: OF ADVERSITY, 23. The text on that page, with Scott's footnote markers stripped, reads: ...lively describing Christian resolution, that saileth in the frail bark of the flesh thorough the waves of the world. But to speak in a mean. The virtue of Prosperity is temperance; the virtue of Adversity is fortitude; which in morals is the more heroical virtue. Prosperity is the blessing of the Old Testament; Adversity is the blessing of the New...

SO BOTH OF MY ATTACKS FAILED, AND THEY FAILED IN DETAIL. First, the capitals: Scott prints lower-case virtue and capital Prosperity and capital Adversity, precisely as the proposal has it, and the verifier's note describes the edition correctly. Second, and this is the one that would have killed the line: in Scott, But to speak in a mean is a sentence of its own, closed with a full stop, so the quotation begins at a genuine sentence head. Nothing is minted, nothing is capitalised to make it look like a sentence, and no ellipsis is owed. The clause which in morals is the more heroical virtue is carried whole and ends in a full stop, as rule 6 requires. The page is right, the wording is right to the semicolon, and the note's account of what other settings do (the 1625 Vertue of Prosperitie and Heroicall Vertue, and the modern texts that run the clause on with commas) matches what I know of them.

OTHER GATES. Of Adversity is Essay V in the 1625 ordering (Of Truth, Of Death, Of Unity in Religion, Of Revenge, Of Adversity), so the essay number is right. shipped.js: shipped empty, near empty, francis bacon at 1 of 3 and that one in May, so he is under the year cap and not twice in this month. Not banned, on no trap in the misattribution list. Scope: 1625, printed 1908, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. Tag Essay is the form of the work in the plainest possible sense. Publishable. Source line is 76 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote. Theme fit is the best in this set: the virtue of Adversity is fortitude is what July is about, and it is counsel a reader can carry out of the room.

ONE COSMETIC POINT, NOT A REFUTATION. Scott's volume is titled The Essays of Francis Bacon, and the source line says only Essays. That is the standard short title for the work and the editor is named in the parenthesis, so a reader can find the page; I would leave it as it stands rather than spend characters on it.
